marble.name: The Rock Cycle
marble.subject: Science
marble.description: Explain the rock cycle: how igneous rocks form from magma, sedimentary rocks from compressed sediment, and metamorphic rocks from heat and pressure, and how all rock types can transform into one another over geological time
marble.prompt: If you picked up a piece of marble on a school trip, could they explain how it was originally limestone, what changed it into marble, and how long that process took?

cluster.summary: Your child is exploring the materials around them — identifying different substances like wood, plastic, and metal, and discovering their properties such as whether they're hard or soft, rough or smooth.

misconceptions: Thinking the rock cycle has a fixed start and runs one way, rather than being a cycle any rock can enter and leave.
Believing metamorphic rock forms by melting, when it forms by heat and pressure WITHOUT melting (melting gives igneous).
Assuming rocks form quickly, missing the geological timescales involved.
Confusing weathering (breakdown in place) with erosion (transport of the fragments).
Thinking each rock type is permanent, rather than able to transform into the others over time.
representations: The rock-cycle wheel/diagram with igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic nodes and process arrows.
Rock-texture cues: interlocking crystals (igneous), layers/fossils (sedimentary), banding (metamorphic).
A crust cross-section showing burial, heat/pressure at depth, and magma rising and cooling.
Example rocks per class (granite, basalt, limestone, sandstone, marble, slate).
A geological-time scale contrasting rock-cycle steps with a human lifetime.
authoredAnswer: Not true — over GEOLOGICAL time (millions of years) rock is continually recycled. Granite could be weathered into grains, the grains compacted into sedimentary rock, then heated and squeezed into metamorphic rock, or melted to magma and cooled into new igneous rock. wrongAnswers.wrong: True — granite stays granite forever; rocks never change into other kinds.
wrongAnswers.revealedBy: denies any rock can become another type; treats rock as fixed
wrongAnswers.fix: Introduce deep time and the cycle: weathering, sedimentation, heat/pressure and melting continually remake rock. Trace one grain through several forms.

wrongAnswers.wrong: Only in one fixed order — igneous first, then sedimentary, then metamorphic, never skipping.
wrongAnswers.revealedBy: recites a single loop and can't describe shortcuts (e.g. metamorphic melting straight back to magma)
wrongAnswers.fix: Show the cycle has many pathways and shortcuts — any type can become any other; it isn't a fixed conveyor. Trace several different routes.

wrongAnswers.wrong: By melting the rock completely and letting it cool again.
wrongAnswers.revealedBy: says heat MELTS rock to make metamorphic rock, not distinguishing it from igneous
wrongAnswers.fix: Metamorphism changes rock by heat AND pressure WITHOUT fully melting (limestone→marble); melting then cooling makes IGNEOUS rock. Contrast the two directly.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: expects rock change to be observable quickly; no sense of millions of years
wrongAnswers.fix: Build deep-time intuition (mountains rise/erode over millions of years); that's why we see snapshots, not the process. Use timeline analogies.
